summary: Jotika Khur-Yearn is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a PhD at SOAS University of London under the supervision of Kate Crosby (attested 2012).

Jowita Kramer is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology who studied at the University of Hamburg (MA under David P. Jackson; PhD under Lambert Schmithausen), Munich (Habilitation), and Göttingen. She became professor at Leipzig in 2021.

Joy Cecile Brennan is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who earned a PhD at the University of Chicago, studying under Paul Mendes-Flohr, Richard Rosengarten, Constance Furey, and Diane Martin.
Juan Wu works in Buddhist studies and Indology, earning a PhD from Cardiff University under Max Deeg (attested 2012) and holding a postdoctoral position at the University of Tokyo (attested 2014).

Judit Törzsök is a scholar of Indology and religious studies who earned an MA at Eötvös Loránd University and a DPhil at the University of Oxford under Alexis Sanderson. She taught at Lille (2001–2017) before joining EPHE in 2018.

Judith Simmer-Brown is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. She studied at Cornell College, Florida State, Columbia, and Walden University (PhD), taught at institutions including Western Washington University (~1974–1976), and joined Naropa University in 1977.
Juhn Y. Ahn is a Buddhist studies scholar who received a PhD from the University of California, Berkeley in 2007 and holds a post at the University of Michigan.
Juhyung Rhi is a scholar of Buddhist studies and art history who earned a PhD at the University of California, Berkeley. In 1992, he became Professor of Art History at Seoul National University.
Juichiro Tanabe is a philosopher who studied as a PhD candidate at the University of Bradford (2000–2001) and studied under Richard Hunn.

Jules Barthélemy-Saint-Hilaire was a scholar of philosophy, Indology, and Buddhist studies who studied at Collège Louis-le-Grand and Bourbon College. He served as professor of Greek at the Collège de France (1838–1852).

Jules Bloch was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Sylvain Lévi and Antoine Meillet at EPHE, INALCO, and the University of Paris. He held chairs at INALCO (1921–1937), EPHE (1919–1951), and the Collège de France (1936–1951).

Jules Brooks Levinson is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology who completed a PhD at the University of Virginia under Jeffrey Hopkins in 1994 and served as assistant professor of religion at Hamline University (attested 1996).

Jules Michelet was a historian educated at Lycée Charlemagne. He served at the École Normale Supérieure, held a section head post at the Archives nationales (1831–1851), and was professor of history at the Collège de France (1838–1852).

Jules Oppert was a linguist and historian who studied at Heidelberg, Bonn, Berlin, and Kiel (PhD ~1847). He served as professor at INALCO (1857) and professor of Assyriology at the Collège de France (1874–1905).

Julia A. B. Hegewald is an Indologist and art historian educated at SOAS (BA, PhD), Oxford (MA), and RWTH Aachen University (Habilitation). She was appointed professor at the University of Bonn in 2010.

Julia Ching was a scholar of Sinology, religious studies, and philosophy who studied at the College of New Rochelle, Catholic University of America, and Australian National University. She joined the University of Toronto as professor in 1978.

Julia F. Andrews is an art historian and Sinologist who studied at Brown University, the University of California, Berkeley, and Harvard University. She took up a post at Ohio State University around 1987.
Julia Leslie was an Indologist and scholar of religious studies who held a post at SOAS University of London from around 1995 to 2004.

Juliane Schober is a scholar of religious studies and Buddhist studies who completed her PhD at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign in 1989 and holds a faculty post at Arizona State University.
Julie Gifford is a scholar of Buddhist studies and religious studies who completed her PhD at the University of Chicago under Frank E. Reynolds and held a post at Miami University.
